key_insight: The paper proposes a principles-based framework for using collaborative AI agents to accelerate experimental physics research without replacing human researchers.
engineering_relevance: For quantum and experimental physics workflows, the framework offers a practical way to use LLM agents for design, control, modeling, and analysis while keeping human oversight and scientific rigor.
method: Define ten requirements spanning scientific norms, agent behavior, and domain expertise
Wrap off-the-shelf LLMs with custom scaffolding for scientific workflows and closed-loop campaigns
Use iterative agent-human loops to pursue a clearly defined experimental goal
evidence_signal: The approach is supported by six experimental physics case studies that produced useful outputs, including better-performing neural-network and defect models, a fabrication-ready microwave waveguide design, improved quantum control pulses, NMR hardware commissioning to ~1 Hz precision, and a new spin-ice reconstruction pipeline.
watch_item: Results depend on careful human direction and domain validation, so agent outputs should not be treated as autonomous or inherently reliable.
paper_title: Principles and Techniques for Agentic Research in Experimental Physics
